title: IFERROR: catch the error, show your text

screens.prompt: In B5, look up the price of the SKU in A4, and show "no price" if the lookup fails.

hints.syntax: Two arguments with a comma between: =IFERROR(what might fail, what to show instead).
hints.func-iferror: The lookup on its own returns #N/A in B5. IFERROR wraps that call and supplies the words.
hints.require-ref: Ask for the code held in A4, so a different SKU changes the answer.
hints.value: TX-109 is not in A2:B3, so B5 should hold the fallback text the prompt names, not the error.
hints.error: IFERROR ends at its closing bracket. Anything added outside it works on the text, and #VALUE! comes back.

reject.why: the closing bracket is missing, so nothing runs
the bare lookup returns #N/A, which is the error this lesson exists to replace
one argument leaves IFERROR with nothing to show when the lookup fails
nothing in that can fail, so the answer is the SKU itself
the fallback is the text you pass, and the prompt asked for no price
the SKU typed into the formula, so asking about another SKU means editing the formula
the fallback text is then added to a number outside the protection, and #VALUE! comes back

docs.explain:
IFERROR takes two arguments: the calculation that might fail, and what to show when it does. Anything that goes wrong inside the first argument is replaced by the second. Here the lookup on TX-109 finds nothing in A2:B3 and would return #N/A, so the cell reads no price instead.

IFERROR catches every error the same way, which is wider than a lookup miss. A reference that no longer points anywhere, or arithmetic on text, gets the same two words as a code that is simply absent. A broken formula then reads like missing data.

Put the guard around the part that can fail. The SKU is read from A4, so a different code changes the answer without touching the formula. Arithmetic left outside the IFERROR still returns an error instead of text.

errors.text: The lookup finds nothing and no fallback is supplied, so the cell shows the error instead of words.
A number is added to the fallback text outside the wrapper, so the whole cell turns into #VALUE!.
The same fallback answers a broken reference too, so a formula fault prints as a missing price and nobody looks.

docs.atWork: A price list sent to a customer, where a discontinued code has to read as missing instead of #N/A.
docs.outcome: Replace a failed lookup with words you chose, and know which faults those words will hide.
docs.dataset: Two prices and a missing SKU

seo.title: IFERROR in Excel: replace an error with text
seo.description: A lookup for TX-109 finds nothing and returns #N/A. IFERROR shows text you choose instead, which reads better and can also hide a real mistake.
